title: Provenance tagging and profile-diff serializer for model release deltas
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: model release notes and performance regressions are hard to audit because we lack canonical provenance fields and a compact, deterministic diff format for performance/profile deltas. This PR introduces structured provenance tagging (who/where/how an artifact was produced + optional signature) and a deterministic profile-diff serializer used by the release assembler and CLI. The serializer produces small, repeatable payloads that make it trivial to compute human-friendly change summaries and automated regression flags.

What I changed (high-level):
- Add `provenance` top-level metadata in model manifests: producer, pipeline_id, git_revision, build_recipe, artifact_hash, signing_key_id (optional).
- Add a `signed_artifacts` boolean and `signatures` list (opaque string tokens) to support downstream audit and private deployments.
- Introduce profile-diff serializer: `profiles/serializer/v1` that emits a deterministic, stable delta (metrics + histograms summarized, quantization/latency knobs) and canonical ordering for keys. This is intentionally compact so it can be attached to release bundles and used by release-notes tooling.
- Wire CLI: `regctl models diff --from <id> --to <id> --format serializer-v1` emits the canonical delta and returns machine+human summary.
- Database migration: add columns `provenance_json` (JSONB) and `signed_artifacts` (bool) + small index on `provenance->>artifact_hash`. Migration is additive and backward-compatible.
- Tests: unit tests for serializer determinism, schema validation for new manifest fields, integration test for CLI path that generates a bundle consumed by the release assembler.
- Release assembler: small hook so that when a model release bundle contains a `serializer-v1` delta we extract and append a human-readable summary to the generated release notes.

Checklist: 
- [x] Schema additions (manifest + DB migration)
- [x] Deterministic serializer implementation
- [x] CLI integration + docs snippet
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Migration verified on staging with historic manifests

Compatibility notes: this is additive; manifests without `provenance` continue to work. The serializer is versioned (v1) to allow future richer deltas. Producers can opt in to signing; private deployments with KMS can store the `signatures` blob.

Small example (serializer output snippet):
{
  "model_id": "m-2026-abc123",
  "delta_id": "d-2026-44291",
  "metrics": [
    {"name": "mean_latency_ms", "from": "12.4", "to": "13.9", "pct_change": "+12.1%"},
    {"name": "p95_latency_ms", "from": "34.0", "to": "31.8", "pct_change": "-6.5%"}
  ],
  "kv": {"quantize_profile": "int8-opt"}
}

Why this change: a deterministic delta lets downstream tooling reliably detect regressions, attribute them to commits/pipelines via the provenance tags, and include compact, auditable artifacts in release bundles. This helps SRE/debugging and supports compliance-friendly deployments.

Related: picks up lessons from ENG-1167 (release assembler) and complements existing profile-calibration work.

release_notes: Add provenance metadata to model manifests and a deterministic profile-diff serializer (v1). Enables artifact signing, deterministic release deltas, and machine-readable change summaries for release notes. Backward-compatible; opt-in signing.
